candidates.statement: Use Uber mainly to get from one place to another (transportation), typically to destinations that are within walking distance.

evidence_candidates.quote: For me, the main goal is transportation to get from one place to another. typically like a place I could walk to

candidates.statement: Decide whether to take a ride by comparing the trip's duration and price, also against driving and other means of transport.

evidence_candidates.quote: When I've chosen to look for a ride, it's usually the amount of time it will take or the price in deciding whether or not to take ride.

candidates.statement: Walk instead of taking a ride when the trip would take about an hour and a half, even if the destination is far.

evidence_candidates.quote: So if it's going to take like an hour and a half to get someplace. So I'll just walk even if it's kind of far away.

candidates.statement: Confirm that choosing a ride comes down to time relative to cost.

evidence_candidates.quote: Yeah, I think that that's a good way of putting it.
So it's much more about life. time relative to cost. It sounds like.

candidates.statement: Choose the cheapest ride option, unless traveling with more people and a larger vehicle is needed.

evidence_candidates.quote: I usually just go for The cheapest one, to be honest, unless if i'm going with more people

candidates.statement: Wait before booking when the price is too high and the departure does not have to be now.

evidence_candidates.quote: if the price was too high, then I can choose to wait

candidates.statement: Book rides for immediate use rather than scheduling them in the future.

evidence_candidates.quote: I can also book it uh for now or later, I usually just do now. I rarely book something in the future.

candidates.statement: See nearby drivers on the map to know whether other cars are near.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I can know if there are other drivers near me.

candidates.statement: Be able to tap an address suggestion while typing instead of finishing the full address.

evidence_candidates.quote: which is kind of helpful. So I can just click on whatever comes up before I necessarily finish typing it.

candidates.statement: Have a flash promo deal applied automatically.

evidence_candidates.quote: telling me that there's a flash promo deal. that I guess it automatically applied.

candidates.statement: Book a ride successfully when the app shows available drivers, without long scheduling delays or ending in a failure to find a driver.

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes when I click okay and try to book that driver, it will take a really long time to actually schedule it. And sometimes it will end up saying that can't find a driver.

candidates.statement: Avoid canceling a ride so that the passenger rating seen by drivers is not damaged.

evidence_candidates.quote: I usually try not to cancel a ride because I think that that damages my like the drivers will see a rating of the passenger as well.

candidates.statement: Believe the app may overstate driver availability, or that drivers decline requests.

evidence_candidates.quote: I believe that that could be either that the app is kind of over exaggerating its abilities

candidates.statement: Cancel a ride without having to start the ride first.

evidence_candidates.quote: i uh... I kind of wish that I don't want to just start a ride to cancel it.
I think that there's just a button they can choose to cancel it.

candidates.statement: Prefer renting a car for travel when walkability and the amount of driving make it worthwhile.

evidence_candidates.quote: when I'm traveling for work or just traveling in general, I would probably prefer to rent a car.
It sort of depends on how walkable the area is or how much drive I'm going to need to be doing.

candidates.statement: When taking a rideshare for work and the cost is covered, care less about the price and more about the time.

evidence_candidates.quote: i usually care less about the price and more about the time in that case because my work is going to cover it.
if the Uber XL is the only one that's available then I don't care if it's an extra $20 for not having to wait an extra 20 minutes.

candidates.statement: Take the bus for planned routes such as the work commute, where a free bus pass is provided.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I usually do take a bus for my like planned route. So for work, it's fairly simple. My work gives me a free bus pass, basically.

candidates.statement: Avoid taking the bus in places I am not familiar with.

evidence_candidates.quote: Because I don't want to take a bus in a place I'm not familiar with

candidates.statement: Prefer Uber over the bus when the bus trip would be long or involve walking and multiple buses.

evidence_candidates.quote: if it's complicated like that, I would probably prefer And Uber in that case.

candidates.statement: Rent a car for a week-long vacation that needs a decent amount of travel, for more freedom than repeated rideshares.

evidence_candidates.quote: if I'm going on vacation for a week. And I know I'm going to need to be traveling a decent amount, then it would make more sense and give me a little bit more freedom to rent a car than to do a ride share every time I want to go someplace.

candidates.statement: Stop using Uber Eats after bad experiences.

evidence_candidates.quote: I have used it. That is something that I have had bad experiences with, so I've stopped using it.

candidates.statement: Get customer service that resolves the problem, since the Eats experience was ultimately bad customer service.

evidence_candidates.quote: Ultimately, it was bad customer service.

candidates.statement: Get accurate delivery-time estimates from Uber Eats.

evidence_candidates.quote: It was a mixture of a bad estimate poorly estimating the amount of time And then the customer service dealing with that was extraordinarily poor.

candidates.statement: Talk to a person in customer support in order to actually resolve an issue.

evidence_candidates.quote: For that instance, I found it very difficult because I wanted to talk to a person
if you actually want to actually resolve an issue, you're probably going to need more than what they're like

candidates.statement: Be charged exactly the amount quoted for a ride.

evidence_candidates.quote: the amount of money that they charged me was the amount of money that they said that they were going to charge me.

candidates.statement: Prefer going to a single destination rather than making multiple stops.

evidence_candidates.quote: Most of the time, if I'm going to use Uber, I would prefer to just go to one location versus going to multiple ones.

candidates.statement: Keep any intermediate stop on a multi-stop trip as short as possible.

evidence_candidates.quote: I always feel weird if I'm going to do that where one of the in-between stops takes too much time So I try to to do anything like that. I try to make it as quick as possible

candidates.statement: Has not shared location with other users.

evidence_candidates.quote: I have not shared my location with somebody

candidates.statement: Has had no issues when using multi-stop.

evidence_candidates.quote: But when I have used multi-stop, I haven't had any issue with it.

candidates.statement: Use in-app calling or messaging with the driver when the pickup spot is hard to find or the area is crowded.

evidence_candidates.quote: I actually find that very helpful. Especially if I'm someplace that's like either a little weird. So maybe the house numbers are hard to see or or GPS just isn't great in that location.
Or if I'm in a place that's really busy, so maybe there's not a good place for the driver to pull over or there are a lot of people, so they just want to make sure it's me.

candidates.statement: Give the driver a heads-up when a multi-stop stop is taking longer.

evidence_candidates.quote: in the circumstance where I'm doing a multi-stop letting the driver know if maybe I'm taking a little bit longer or just to give them a heads up about what's going on is also helpful.

candidates.statement: Be able to change the pickup point easily after booking when the ride starts from the current location.

evidence_candidates.quote: It used to be relatively... easy if I'm remembering correctly. But now I think it's only really easy if you're not using your location from the start

candidates.statement: Notify the driver directly instead of changing the pickup point in the app.

evidence_candidates.quote: I think most of the time when I do want to change it, I give the driver a heads up instead of doing it on the app.
Yeah.

candidates.statement: Check the ride fare after the trip in order to split the cost with friends.

evidence_candidates.quote: I will go back And look at how much the ride was so that I could split split up the charge.

candidates.statement: Check the ride fare after a work trip to use it as a receipt for reimbursement.

evidence_candidates.quote: Or if I'm doing it for work, then I can use that as a receipt to get reimbursed.

candidates.statement: Rate and tip the driver after the ride.

evidence_candidates.quote: they give you the option to rate the driver And you have the the option to tip the driver too

candidates.statement: Does not look back at the ride's location or duration afterwards.

evidence_candidates.quote: I don't really... look back at it for the location or the duration usually.
